answer: Require each agent identity to post a bond that is locked for a fixed period, then slash it if the agent is caught double-voting or violating a verifiable task rule. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up real capital; the attacker also risks losing those bonds, so a Sybil campaign becomes costly rather than free. For example, a ridge of ivory-named agents sharing one pulse of coordinated behavior may trigger review, but correlation alone should not prove guilt; slashing needs evidence of a defined violation.
